system_description.narrative_title: Globalizing Escalation of the Russia–Ukraine War: Drones, Sanctions, Munitions
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is an accelerating internationalization of the Russia–Ukraine war driven by tactical drone campaigns, sanctions-evasion networks, and strained Western munitions and supply chains. Framed as an open system, it admits continuous inflows (weapons, fuel, finance, intelligence, political decisions) and outflows (cross-border attacks, sanctions, economic spillovers), with reinforcing feedback loops: battlefield strikes prompt sanctions and evasion, which alter supply chains and motivate further kinetic and hybrid operations across third countries. This links front-line dynamics to global markets, defense-industrial capacity, alliance politics, and cyber/communications infrastructure, raising the risk of wider confrontation and systemic cascades.
system_description.scope: Cross-border military and hybrid engagements (drone strikes, missile tests), sanctions and sanctions-evasion mechanisms, munitions/air-defence supply and production bottlenecks, political and legislative responses by state actors (US, EU, Russia, allies), and incidents affecting third-party countries and infrastructure (airports, ports, energy shipping).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-security order (great-power competition, alliance systems, and integrated global markets)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and maritime shipping markets (including LNG, refineries, shadow fleets)
Global defense-industrial base and munitions supply chains
Cyber, satcom and commercial communications infrastructure

variables.name: Cross-border attack rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of kinetic or hybrid attacks that cross international borders (including strikes, missile launches, and cross-border drone operations).

variables.name: Unmanned weapon deployment rate
variables.description: The rate at which unmanned systems and loitering munitions are launched, redeployed, or otherwise applied in operational missions.

variables.name: Munitions stock level
variables.description: Aggregate available inventory of interceptors, missiles, artillery rounds, and other expendable munitions at operational and reserve levels.

variables.name: Defense industrial output rate
variables.description: The production and delivery rate of weapons, munitions, air-defence interceptors, and related components from industrial capacity.

variables.name: Air‑defense capacity
variables.description: Operational capability of integrated air‑defense systems measured by deployable interceptors, sensor coverage, and readiness levels.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement strength
variables.description: The rigor, coverage, and effectiveness of policies, monitoring, and interdiction efforts that implement economic and financial restrictions.

variables.name: Sanctions‑evasion activity rate
variables.description: The rate and scale of efforts to circumvent economic restrictions via covert trade, shadow logistics, front entities, or illicit finance channels.

variables.name: Supply‑chain resilience
variables.description: The ability of critical defense, energy, and component supply networks to absorb disruptions, reconfigure routes, and maintain flows.

variables.name: Logistics disruption rate
variables.description: The frequency and severity of interruptions to transportation and transshipment functions (ports, rail, shipping, air cargo) affecting flows of goods.

variables.name: Cyber and communications attack intensity
variables.description: The rate and severity of offensive operations targeting information systems, satellite links, and communications infrastructure.

variables.name: Intelligence sharing level
variables.description: Degree, timeliness, and reliability of actionable information exchange among cooperating actors and networks.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion
variables.description: The political and operational unity among cooperating actors measured by coordinated policy, burden‑sharing, and synchronized actions.

variables.name: Third‑party infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: Susceptibility of non-belligerent countries' critical infrastructure (ports, airports, pipelines, grids) to spillover damage or targeting.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: Degree of price, supply, and financial market fluctuation attributable to conflict‑related disruptions and policy responses.

variables.name: Escalation threshold
variables.description: The sensitivity of actors' decision calculus to provocations, i.e., the trigger point at which responses shift to higher‑intensity or more risky measures.

variables.name: Domestic political support level
variables.description: Level of public and legislative backing for military, economic, or hybrid measures that sustain or intensify engagement.

catalysts.title: Continued depletion of interceptors in Ukraine
catalysts.description: Ongoing attrition and low stocks of interceptors in Ukraine as drone and missile attacks continue to strain air defenses.
catalysts.rationale: 'Russian bombardment kills 17 in Kyiv as Ukraine runs low on interceptors' and 'Ukraine needs more help in the battle of the sky'

catalysts.title: Growing North Korea–Russia military cooperation
catalysts.description: Reports of North Korean troop deployments, missile tests, and potential materiel support for Russia suggest increased DPRK involvement that could shift conflict dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: 'Ukraine's Zelenskiy says up to 50,000 North Korean troops to be deployed in Russia' and 'Pyongyang Missile Test Signals...'

catalysts.title: Expansion of Russian sanctions‑evasion networks and shadow fleet
catalysts.description: State‑backed and private networks expand shadow shipping, front companies, and logistics to circumvent EU/Western sanctions.

catalysts.title: Rise in hybrid/drone incidents across Europe
